FX-BLOOM-001.says: Threshold 80, radius 4, no streaks: only the yellow patch, whose brightest channel is 98 %, blooms; the brown at 60 % and the purple do not, though the halo reaches the brown. The halo is brightest close to the yellow and fades into the empty space round it.

FX-BLOOM-003.says: Radius 0: nothing spreads, and each yellow pixel is added onto itself, twice as bright.

FX-BLOOM-004.says: Threshold 100: nothing is that bright, so the drawing is untouched.

FX-BLOOM-005.says: Threshold 60: the brown, at exactly 60 %, blooms too.

FX-BLOOM-006.says: Radius 0 with a cross of streaks, length 6, angle 0: the yellow's light runs straight up and down and straight left and right, and nowhere else: above the patch it is lit, off its corners it is not.

FX-BLOOM-007.says: The same with a star: four lines, so the diagonals off the patch's corners are lit too, and the straight lines are half as strong, as the light is shared among four lines, not two.

FX-BLOOM-008.says: A cross at angle 45: the streaks run along the diagonals only.

FX-BLOOM-009.says: A cross at angle 90: the same two lines as angle 0, each walked the other way, so this is FX-BLOOM-006 to rounding.

FX-BLOOM-010.says: The defaults, threshold 80, radius 20, intensity 1, no streaks: a halo wider than the whole drawing.

FX-BLOOM-011.says: The defaults with a star of streaks, length 60.

FX-BLOOM-012.says: Radius 4, a cross of length 6, intensity 2.5: two and a half times as strong, and where it adds past white it is not cut off.

FX-BLOOM-013.says: The patches half covering: the yellow blooms as in FX-BLOOM-001, at half the strength.

FX-BLOOM-014.says: Radius keyed from 0 at frame 0 to 8 at frame 4, linear: frame 0 is FX-BLOOM-003, frame 2 is FX-BLOOM-001, frame 4 is radius 8.

FX-BLOOM-015.says: Length keyed from 0 at frame 0 to 12 at frame 4, radius 0, a cross: frame 0 is each yellow pixel added onto itself twice over, frame 2 is FX-BLOOM-006.

FX-BLOOM-016.says: Angle keyed from 0 at frame 0 to 90 at frame 4, radius 0, a cross: frame 0 is FX-BLOOM-006, frame 2 is FX-BLOOM-008, and frame 4 is FX-BLOOM-006 again.

FX-BLOOM-017.says: Threshold keyed from 100 at frame 0 to 20 at frame 4, linear: frame 0 is the drawing, frame 4 has the purple blooming too.

FX-BLOOM-018.says: Radius 4 and a cross of length 6, moved three pixels right: the bloom is done on the drawing before it is moved, and the streak that ran past the drawing's left edge now shows in columns 0 to 2.

FX-BLOOM-019.says: Radius 2.5 and length 2.5: neither is rounded.

FX-BLOOM-020.says: Threshold 101, above 100. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-BLOOM-021.says: Radius 501, above 500. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-BLOOM-022.says: Radius -1, below 0. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-BLOOM-023.says: Intensity 11, above 10. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-BLOOM-024.says: Length 501, above 500. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-BLOOM-025.says: Angle 3601, above 3600. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-BLOOM-026.says: Radius keyed to 600 at frame 4. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-BLOOM-027.says: Streaks "rays", which is not none, cross or star. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-BLOOM-028.says: Streaks "Cross", with a capital: words are matched exactly. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.
